summary: Start from strings and build up to loops, functions, lists, dicts, tuples, f-strings, files, exceptions, and debugging. Every lesson uses real GPS NMEA sentences, the same data you parsed in EECE5554, so by the end you can write a GPS log parser yourself.

lessonTitles.m00.l04: 0.4 for loops and the NMEA checksum

project.title: NMEA log analyzer
hints: Break it into small functions you already wrote in the lessons: validate one line, parse one GGA, then loop over lines.
Count three things as you loop: total lines, lines with a bad checksum or format, and valid GGA fixes by quality. A dict is perfect for counting by quality.

Pseudocode: for each line in the file: strip it; skip if blank; if checksum invalid: bad += 1, continue; if it's GGA: parse it, update counts and min/max satellites. After the loop, build and return the summary dict.
project.resumeBullet: Wrote a Python NMEA 0183 log analyzer that validates XOR checksums, parses GGA fixes, and reports fix-quality statistics, tested with N pytest cases including corrupted and empty-field input.
